items.new: Finally, I always go to sea as a sailor because of the healthy exercise and pure air of the forecastle deck. For as in this world headwinds are far more common than winds from astern (that is, if you never violate the Pythagorean maxim), so for the most part the Commodore on the quarter-deck gets his air secondhand from the sailors on the forecastle. He thinks he breathes it first; but not so. In much the same way the common people lead their leaders in many other things, while the leaders little suspect it. But why it was that, after repeatedly smelling the sea as a merchant sailor, I should now take it into my head to go on a whaling voyage — that the invisible police officer of the Fates, who keeps me under constant surveillance, secretly dogs my steps, and influences me in some unaccountable way, can answer better than anyone else. And no doubt my going on this whaling voyage formed part of the grand program of Providence that was drawn up a long time ago. It came in as a sort of brief interlude and solo between more extensive performances. I take it that this part of the playbill must have run something like this:

items.new: A short time passed, and up into this silence came Ahab, alone, from his cabin. Taking a few turns on the quarter-deck, he paused to gaze over the side; then, slowly climbing into the main-chains, he took Stubb's long spade — still lying there after the whale's beheading — and, striking it into the lower part of the half-suspended mass, he placed its other end like a crutch under one arm, and so stood leaning over, his eyes intently fixed on this head.
